source.title: Towards Precise Scaling Laws for Video Diffusion Transformers
source.authors: Yuanyang Yin; Ya-Qi Zhao; Mingwu Zheng; Ke Lin; Jia-Rong Ou; Rui Chen; Victor Shea-Jay Huang; Jia-Hao Wang; Xin Tao; Peng-Fei Wan; Di Zhang; Baoqun Yin; Wentao Zhang; Kun Gai

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some equations and figure text have extraction/formatting artifacts, but the reported experiments and results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study refines scaling-law claims for video diffusion transformers: it reports that fixed suboptimal hyperparameters reduce fitting and compute-optimal allocation accuracy, and fits laws using optimized hyperparameters. This is a refinement in a new modality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own validation-loss scaling fits, large-model extrapolations, and compute-allocation results for video DiT, plus image DiT results in the supplement. It does not report downstream task benchmarks, architecture-shape comparisons, or experiments on repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. Language-model results in the paper are cited background, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study fits its own validation-loss power laws in parameters and tokens for video diffusion transformers, plus a one-frame image variant. It runs IsoFLOP compute-optimal experiments and checks extrapolations to larger runs. It argues that fixed suboptimal batch size and learning rate distort both the loss fit and the compute-optimal split. This bears on V2, V3, V5 and V7 in a new modality and refines how the laws should be fitted. No language-model results are its own.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors confirm that video DiTs exhibit scaling laws and propose power laws for optimal batch size and learning rate in N and T. They argue that using these optimal hyperparameters gives precise loss and optimal-size predictions, whereas fixed suboptimal settings overestimate the optimal model size. They note limits: constant learning rate only, validation loss only, and small low-resolution models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses power-law fitting of validation loss against model size and training tokens and compute-optimal allocation, but applies it to video/image diffusion transformers rather than language models and explicitly fits optimal batch size and learning rate. Uses validation loss, not language-model cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss-fit MSE and predicted-versus-empirical optimal-model-size slope discrepancy differ between optimal and fixed suboptimal batch-size/learning-rate settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The study fits power laws for the optimal batch size and learning rate as functions of N and T, and validates them by grid search at 1.07B. For video, Bopt ∝ T^0.808·N^0.191 and ηopt ∝ T^-0.045·N^-0.162.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal batch size and learning rate follow predictable power laws in model size and training tokens.

record.problems: The experiments use a 2000-sample validation subset and focus on validation loss rather than external video-quality benchmarks. The authors note that they only fit constant learning rates, study smaller low-resolution models, and do not test how resolution or frame rate affects the scaling law. Architecture depth and width are scaled proportionally, so architecture-shape invariance is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable reported result was left out. Figure-only hyperparameter-grid values for the 1.07B video model are not included because the text does not provide their numeric values.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured; all results are for video and image DiT.
Width and depth are scaled proportionally (d/nlayer = 128), and no shape comparison is made at a fixed parameter count.
Repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested, nor are other resolutions or frame rates.
No downstream or video-quality benchmarks are used; validation loss only.
Parameter-counting conventions, learning-rate schedules (constant learning rate only), data and fitting method are not varied.

missing.what: Empirical IsoFLOP compute-optimal fit under optimal hyperparameters: Nopt = 1.5787·C^0.4146. Row r4 mislabels the predicted fit as this one.
Fixed-suboptimal compute-optimal fits: empirical Nopt = 0.0130·C^0.5224 and predicted 9.5521·C^0.3643. The exponent shifts from 0.41 to 0.52 with the hyperparameter choice.
Fixed-suboptimal L(T,N) fit exponents αT = 0.2515 and αN = 0.4101, versus 0.2917 and 0.3188 under optimal hyperparameters.
At 1e10 TFLOPs, the suboptimal-hyperparameter law overestimates the optimal model size; the optimal law gives 39.9% fewer parameters at similar loss.

record.verdict_notes: Under optimal hyperparameters, Nopt grows about as C^0.41–0.43 and Topt about as C^0.57. Data therefore grows faster than model size, matching neither Kaplan nor Hoffmann; this is relevant context for V3 and V7 across modalities. Extrapolation in parameters is only about 4x. Tranche T3 (new setting) would also be defensible.

versions.untested_parts: Tests video and image diffusion transformers, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
Tests extrapolation in video and image diffusion transformers, not language-model runs.
Tests compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for video DiT, not language models or the Kaplan-versus-Hoffmann predictions in language-model training.
The study scales width and depth proportionally rather than comparing architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests video and one-frame image diffusion transformers; does not test repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance is measured.

Tests sensitivity to optimal versus fixed suboptimal batch size and learning rate in this setup; does not systematically vary parameter-counting conventions, data, training schedules, or fitting methods.

relation.reason: Its own experiments fit validation-loss laws, test larger-run predictions, estimate compute-optimal allocation, and compare hyperparameter settings.

tranche.reason: The study shows that fixed suboptimal hyperparameters distort fitted laws and compute-optimal allocation, requiring qualification by training setup. It also supplies new-setting video and image results.

source_check.notes: Equation 22 repeats the predicted allocation formula under an ambiguous optimal-size label; Equation 14 is the empirical fit. Equation 23 is derived rather than an independent token-allocation measurement; image extrapolation does not establish V2's orders-of-magnitude requirement.

statements.correction: Video test: 0.72B parameters, 140B tokens, 5.85e20 FLOPs, 0.15% loss deviation. Largest IsoFLOP fitting budget: 6e18 FLOPs. Comparisons: optimal versus fixed batch size 128 and learning rate 2.5313e-4. No uncertainty intervals reported.
statements.problem: The video loss error and comparison with the largest fitted IsoFLOP budget are correct. The assertion that the study reports no controls overlooks its explicit optimal-versus-fixed-suboptimal hyperparameter comparisons.

statements.correction: T denotes total training tokens, with T = BS in Section 3.2. Dataset: Panda-70M. No separate unique-data and repetition variables, controlled reuse experiment, or explicit exclusion of repetition is reported.
statements.problem: The paper does not provide the joint unique-data/repetition test, but the supplied text does not explicitly exclude repetition.
